correctness.rationale: A fixed adjacent pair is present with probability 1/(2n-1); conditional on its presence, deleting that simple chord leaves a uniform matching on 2n-2 endpoints and does not alter the crossing count of the remainder. This proves the Palm identity exactly. Deleting the chord containing a distinguished endpoint from an unconditional uniform matching couples X_{n-1} below X_n. The covariance, simple-chord variance, and correlation then follow from exact algebra and the established exact crossing variance.

value.rationale: Simple chords and crossings are canonical local and global observables of a random chord diagram and are the two headline statistics of the closest probability treatment. The result gives a finite exact bridge between their Poisson and Gaussian marginal regimes, strengthens the first covariance to all monotone transforms, and produces the unusually clean exact correlation -sqrt(5/(n+3)).
